verdict.rationale: Steel documents a Sessions API that spins up isolated browser instances on demand, plus a session lifecycle API with programmatic create (including custom IDs). It also publishes an OpenAPI spec and a CLI that starts and stops sessions, and markets itself as a way to 'control fleets of browsers in the cloud.' The evidence never states concurrency limits or quotas, which is an explicit part of the story. missing for 10: documented concurrency limits/quotas per plan, explicit evidence of running many sessions in parallel, independent or hands-on corroboration of fleet-scale operation.
